M1.reason: Outline matches the brief's words in the side, front and back views: a squat, rounded yellowish body with the head on a short neck at the front, a tapered rear, dorsal spines, and three limbs reaching the floor. The front limbs are a little stouter than the thin rear leg, but the outline does not break from the brief.

M2.reason: Measured: length 51.4 against the asked 49 (about 5% over), height 46 against the asked 45 (about 2% over). Both are within 15% of the brief's size; the brief gives no width, so width is not scored against it.

M3.reason: Named parts all present: three legs in front, back and side views (a centre leg and two claw-tipped limbs), one large red eye on the front of the head (front and front-left views), and striped and dappled markings on the body (side and back views). The spiked back is not named by the brief and not shown by all three Valve models in the line-up, so its absence is not charged. The leg thickness is charged under M1, not here.

M4.reason: The brief asks for a yellowish body, and the body is a tan-yellow throughout. The eye's red and yellow and the maroon markings are plausible for the described hide. No region reads as a wrong material.

M5.reason: The striped and dappled hide is there: maroon chevron streaks and round spots across the flanks and back (side, right and back-left views), at a sharpness that matches the rest of the model. The streaks are closer to chevrons than plain stripes, but they read as striped and dappled.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric for the line-up test, measured apart. In the four readings the asset was picked as the odd one out once (reading 3, asset at B) and missed in the other three, so the test does not show a fault.

M7.reason: Upright, with the large eye on the front of the head facing the front view camera, and the body rests on its legs with the feet on the floor line in the motion strip. The front is the eye side.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. Triangles are 866: under twice the median of Half-Life's creatures (576, so under 1152) and above the third quartile (740), which is within the rule. Nothing is open or floating in the views given: the underside in the below view is closed, and the feet meet the floor in the motion strip.

C1.reason: Across the 28 frames of the run, the head, neck, body, spikes and limbs stay on the body and move with it. The claw-tipped limbs keep their contact with the floor line, and nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The brief gives no motion of its own, so the run is judged as it stands.
